summary: Dutchess County, NY International Derrick fire tower near the Stissing Mountain summit; restored by Friends of Stissing Landmarks and open to the public.

facts.design: International Derrick steel fire tower (register: Model 1933, 86 ft high; Wikipedia: E-4898, 79 ft 6 in)

staffing.status: fire observation tower until April 1971 per the register, or until between 1979 and 1982 per Wikipedia; not currently staffed as a lookout in these sources

access.note: Wikipedia says the restored tower is open to the public via hiking trails (as of 2023); the register says the Friends maintain it for public use year round, free of charge

visit.trail_note: reached by hiking trails near the summit, per Wikipedia

events.note: Wikipedia: built in late 1933 by the Boston Corners CCC Camp; the register instead gives 1934
register gives 1934 as the build year and says the tower opened that year
in service as a fire observation tower from March 1935 (register); first staffed in 1935, reporting 91 fires and 610 visitors (Wikipedia)
register: in service through April 1971. Wikipedia says lookout operations ceased between 1979 and 1982, so the end date is unresolved
Friends of Stissing Landmarks incorporated in 1989; ownership transferred from New York State in May 1989
restored for the first time; one acre beneath the tower transferred from the Nature Conservancy to the Friends in May 1993
subsequent restoration began in 2017 and was expected to be completed in 2018

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikipedia says the tower was built in late 1933 by the Boston Corners CCC Camp. The register gives 1934 as the build year and says the tower opened that year. The story reports both.
The register says the tower stands 86 feet high. Wikipedia says 79 feet, six inches (24.23 m). The story reports both and does not choose one.
The register says the tower was in service through April 1971. Wikipedia says lookout operations ceased sometime between 1979 and 1982. The story reports both and does not choose one.

notes_for_editor: Only two sources could be read. The Friends of Stissing Landmarks site (stissingfiretower.org/history and the home page) rendered no text, and the New Pine Plains Herald article on the stair and landing replacement (completed October 24, year not visible) returned no body text, so neither is cited. The nysffla.org fire tower list returned 404 on the URL tried, and a search showed an alphabetical list at nysffla.org/alphalist.html that was not read. The story stops at the page-read budget. The register and Wikipedia conflict on the build year (1933 vs 1934), the height (86 ft vs 79 ft 6 in), and the end of lookout service (April 1971 vs 1979-1982). Those are unresolved and need the FOSL history page, the Herald article, or the nysffla list to settle. The register's 2017-2018 restoration is described as expected, so current completion is unverified. The story does not state the restored tower's current hours. The brief's events are kept as they stand: '1934 built' is supported by the register's Built field and the opening date, and the Wikipedia date is noted as a conflict.
